feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
entry.summary: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

entry.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
entry.summary: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

entry.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
entry.summary: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.

entry.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
entry.summary: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.

entry.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
entry.summary: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

entry.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
entry.summary: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?

entry.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
entry.summary: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

entry.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
entry.summary: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

entry.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
entry.summary: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?

entry.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
entry.summary: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.
